question: Conjunctival pallor is considered the most reliable single site for detecting anaemia on physical examination, whereas palmar crease pallor is more specific for moderate-to-severe anaemia (Hb < 9 g/dL).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Recall the examination hierarchy: conjunctivae are the most reliable (skin pigmentation independent). Palmar crease pallor is a specific indicator of significant anaemia (Hb < 9 g/dL). Nail bed and tongue pallor are additional confirmatory sites.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The conjunctivae are consistently vascularised regardless of skin pigmentation, making them the most reliable site. Palmar crease pallor (creases pale as skin when hand is stretched) indicates Hb typically below 9 g/dL — a specific but less sensitive sign.
